Assignee and this claim are both written by the **PM seat**. ⛔ The dev inherits both, confirms the newest `Claim:` names its branch, posts **no** second `Claim:`, and ⛔ never writes the assignee or yields the card.

### Pre-dispatch checks this seat ran

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| open PRs touching either gate or `plugin-markdown.mdx` | **0 of 15** — swept every open PR by files API |
| base at dispatch | `origin/main` = `0f3d15314defc9ef0a52cb3233708f1923337963` |

### ⭐ Triage's one declared unmeasured leg — ANSWERED here, and the answer changes the work

Triage wrote, honestly, that its search for *「a third same-meaning predicate spelled differently」* returned empty but that its escaping was suspect, so ⛔ it would not count that zero as a reading, and asked the dev to re-confirm.

Re-run by this seat on `0f3d15314d`, matched lines printed:

```
scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs:179            const fence = /^([ \t]*)(`{3,}|~{3,})([^\n]*)\n/gm;
scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs:1148     const fence = /^\s*```(\S*)\s*$/.exec(lines[i]);
scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs:680  const fence = /^\s*```(\S*)\s*$/.exec(lines[i]);
```

⇒ **A third predicate DOES exist**, and ⭐ **it is already the correct one.** `keepFencedCodeOnly` in `body-dialect-census.mjs` handles runs of three-or-more, both markers, and closes on *a run at least as long* — its own comment says so verbatim: `// Find the closing fence: same marker character, at least as long.`

⇒ This is exactly triage's option **A**, i.e. the CommonMark rule, **already implemented in this repository**. ⛔ Do not invent it: read it first, and say whether the fix should reuse it, extract it, or deliberately diverge from it — and if diverge, why.

⚠️ ⛔ That does **not** discharge the re-confirmation. Three is what *this* spelling-based search found; triage's warning stands that the discriminant must be 「does this code decide whether a line OPENS a fence」, ⛔ not a regex's spelling. `scripts/` has **25** files mentioning `fence`. Re-derive the population behaviourally and report it with a control.

### Rulings carried as binding

- ✅ **A**, ⛔ C is self-rejected by the card's own sentence (the affected page is *legitimately* teaching nested fences; C would ban a valid form to make the tool's life easier). **B may land WITH A but ⛔ never INSTEAD of A** — B converts a silent mis-parse into a loud one while leaving the greedy `(\S*)` construct in place.
- ⭐ **The two identical copies must not simply both be patched.** Give them a single authority, or a two-way pin that fails when they diverge, with each site naming the other. ⚠️ If their module boundaries make extraction genuinely too costly, ⛔ do not force it — take the pin and **stop and say which case it was**.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9332, reviewed against the DIFF and the repo, ⛔ not against the report

`domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, round R56, 2026-09-13T00:58Z. Head `a65a5dc1a6`, draft, **7 files +483/−23**.

### The fix takes A, and ⭐ folds B **structurally** rather than adding it as a check

`scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs` (new, the single authority):

```js
:87   const MARKER_RUN  = /^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/;
:90   const CLOSING_RUN = /^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*$/;
:117  if (marker === '`' && info.includes('`')) return null;
```

⭐ **Line 117 is the whole of option B, done as structure.** A backtick-bearing info string is **not an opener at all**, so `` `markdown `` is now *unrepresentable* rather than *detectable after it has already been counted* — the module's own comment says exactly that. ⇒ this is the repair order triage made binding (remove the construct that permits the error → make the correct form the only spelling → only then add a check), ⛔ not B substituted for A.

`closesFence` requires the same marker character, a run **at least as long**, and no info string. Its self-test pins both directions, which is what makes it the CommonMark rule rather than half of it:

```
a three-backtick line does NOT close a four-backtick fence  -> false
...nor does a bare three-backtick line                      -> false
a four-backtick line closes a three-backtick fence          -> true
```

### Both copies are gone, verified in the tree ⛔ not in the report

| gate | old spelling `` const fence = /^\s*```(\S*)\s*$/ `` | now |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `check-doc-component-types.mjs` | **0** | `:209 import { closesFence, openFence } from './markdown-fence-scan.mjs';` |
| `check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` | **0** | `:219` same import |

Each site also carries `⛔ Never re-spell the fence predicate here.`

### ⭐ The fork was EXTRACTION, and I checked it was the cheap case rather than a forced one

Triage allowed a two-way pin if the module boundaries made extraction too costly, and required the dev to **say which case it was**. It said extraction, because the gates already share a boundary. Confirmed on `origin/main`:

```
scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs:217
    import { APP_DOCS, appDocsDirs, ROOT_PAGES } from './check-doc-component-types.mjs';
```

⇒ They already import from each other (objectui#7878). There was nothing to force. ✅

⭐ And the recurrence guard is built the right way round: it masks comments with `js-comment-mask.mjs` first — *prose about a regex is not a regex* — then fails if either gate source contains an anchored fence-matching regex literal of its own. **With a positive control**: `it('the guard would catch the predicate that was removed')`, so a guard that stopped matching anything cannot pass by describing nothing. ⚠️ Pleasing detail: that masker is the one PR objectui#9322 routed 29 files onto **earlier this same shift**.

### ⛔ A correction to MY dispatch — the population number I supplied was a floor

My claim comment handed over three predicates and warned the discriminant must be behavioural. The dev re-derived it and the answer is **17 opener-deciding sites**, not 3:

- 15 were already run-aware;
- **2** are the defective pair this card names — ⇒ my figure was **correct about which copies carry the DEFECT**;
- **2 more are not run-aware** and had been missed by every spelling search so far: `check-prompt-component-keys.mjs:176` (`` /^\s*(?:```|~~~)/ ``, a prefix toggle) and `check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` (a non-greedy pair). Both measured **latent today**, filed bare as **objectui#9331**, ⛔ not fixed here.

⭐ The sweep carried its own control: the same command that produced the 17 also printed all three predicates I had named, so the count is a reading and ⛔ not a false zero. 67 files under `scripts/` mention 「fence」; 19 carry a marker literal; the discriminant cuts those to 17. An **indirect** sweep (backtick identifier, `\u0060`, `fromCharCode(96)`) found no opener-deciding site, closing the spelling-independent hatch.

### The lit control — triage's leg, and the one that proves the SHAPE

Acceptance 2 required an **odd** stray-marker fixture, because the real corpus has an even count and resynchronises by accident. Delivered and **pinned as permanent tests over BOTH gates**, not measured once:

| | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| carriage | 5 fences, languages `json` / `` ``markdown `` / `json` / ``` `` ``` / `plaintext`; a prose paragraph read as fence BODY; the last node **invisible**; file ends in an **unterminated** fence | 3 fences, `json` / `markdown` / `json`; the node inside a scanned fence with the right body; **0** unterminated; **0** backtick-bearing languages |
| component-types | 2 type sites + an unterminated report at EOF | 3 type sites at the right lines, 3 code blocks, no unterminated report |

### ⭐ Acceptance 1 — the dev corrected the acceptance instead of satisfying its letter, and it is right

The acceptance (mine, relaying the card) said lines 152–154 must be seen as inside the **inner fence**. Under CommonMark **there is no inner fence there**: the inner markers are literal body text of the four-backtick fence, which is why the body reads **5 lines**, not 3.

```
before:  line=150 lang="`markdown" ok=true bodyLines=0   +  a phantom at 155
after:   line=150 lang="markdown"  ok=false bodyLines=5  — the inner opener, the 3 JS lines, the inner closer
```

⇒ The substance holds (the JavaScript is no longer outside every fence) and the wording of my acceptance was wrong about the mechanism. ⛔ Saying so beats quietly satisfying a mis-stated criterion.

⭐ **Whole-corpus diff of BOTH scanners' output, before vs after: exactly three lines** — two phantom fences replaced by one real fence, `codeBlocks` 1107 → 1106, `typeSites` unchanged at 897. No other fence, site or counter moved. That is the blast radius measured rather than asserted.

### ⭐ And the ablation was declared VOID rather than counted

The first attempt's `EXIT=1` came from a perl escaping error that left the module **unparseable** — a syntax error measuring nothing. ⇒ reported as **void, not as a red**, and redone with exact-anchor edits: 7 failed / 9 passed, the reds including both gate-level desync pins and the corpus invariant; restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, blob byte-identical, 16/16 green.

⚠️ An exit code that comes from the harness rather than the subject is not a reading. Declaring it is the standard this lane wants.

⭐ `pnpm type-check:scripts` was run **by name**, noted as separate from per-package `type-check` — the exact gap that sent PR objectui#9322 back this shift.

### ⛔ NOT armed

CI on `a65a5dc1a6` at this reading: **22 success · 3 skipped · 10 in_progress · 0 failing**. ⛔ Every check, not the required subset — and the flip will add `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, so this green is not the green that authorises the queue. The landing probe will be written **before** the merge and posted then.

It is ⛔ deliberately **out of scope here**; converting it in passing would have widened the PR past its ruling. This leg makes that restraint checkable rather than promised.

### ⛔ Leg 1 — the fault is this seat's, and it is the SECOND instance of the same trap tonight

The one surviving occurrence is:

```
scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs:15:  *     const fence = /^\s*```(\S*)\s*$/.exec(line);
```

Read in context, it is **line 15 of the new module's own docblock**, under the heading *「## The defect this module exists to make unrepresentable」*, quoting verbatim the predicate it replaced. ⇒ **prose, not a call site.**

Re-measured with the **code-only reader this lane's own doctrine mandates** (`grep -vE '^\s*(\*|//|/\*)'`), per file:

| file | pre | post |

⇒ **The fact leg 1 was measuring HOLDS. My expression for measuring it did not.** I wrote a bare `grep -F` and omitted the comment filter that my own doctrine names in the same breath as 「print matched lines, never bare counts」.

⭐ **This is the second time this shift that one of my probe legs was wrong while the work was right** — the first was `### C.` as a must-STAY-ABSENT `0 → 0` leg on objectui#9145, caught *before* the merge by counting on the base. ⚠️ And note what nearly happened: a seat that reads 「leg 1 missed」 and writes the PR up as suspect would have defamed a correct change. The leg that *disproves* a defect and the leg that *mis-measures* one look identical until you print the matched line. ⇒ ⭐ **printing the matched line is not a presentation nicety, it is what separates the two.**
